correctness.rationale: For every integer q>=2, exact edge classification gives q diagonal vertices of degree q and q(q-1) off-diagonal vertices of degree 2, with strong connectivity proved using two-edge paths through diagonal vertices. The unique edge 000 normalizes cyclic rotation. Directed BEST gives N_q=T_q((q-1)!)^q. A two-by-two off-diagonal Laplacian block of determinant 3 for each unordered letter pair, followed by a 2/3-scaled complete-graph Laplacian Schur complement, gives T_q=2^(q-1)3^((q-1)(q-2)/2)q^(q-2). Independent exact integer determinants at q=2..6, and two separately programmed exhaustive Euler-tour enumerators at q=2,3, corroborate the full symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The pre-existing literature motivates restricted universal cycles of noninjective words and establishes existence but does not quantify how many distinct efficient cyclic encodings are available at the first length-three case. A closed all-q product is a natural complete enumeration, not a narrow arbitrary table. The factor 3 from each off-diagonal state pair and the exact complete-graph determinant expose a reusable structural decomposition, giving all alphabet sizes rather than a single numerical increment.
